chore: skip Z3 build if upstream has no newer release

In do_update_z3, before building, query the latest release tag from
Z3Prover/z3 and compare it (via sort -V) against the version currently
tracked in z3_version.rb. If the installed version is already current
or newer, print a message and return without building.

commit.message:
chore: always check GitHub Release before early-exit in do_update_z3

Previously, do_update_z3 returned 0 ("nothing to do") immediately when
the upstream Z3 version was not newer than the current version, without
first checking whether the GitHub Release actually exists on
riscv/riscv-unified-db.

Restructure the logic so that:
- The version comparison determines the target_version to build/release
  (latest_version if upstream is newer, current_version otherwise)
- The GitHub Release existence check is always performed for that
  target_version before any early exit
- Only if the release already exists does the function return 0

This ensures that if the release was never created (e.g. the upload
step failed in a prior run), re-running 'chore update z3' will build
and create it even when the version hasn't changed upstream.

commit.message:
chore: use XDG cache libs when creating release for current Z3 version

When do_update_z3 needs to create a missing GitHub Release for the
already-current Z3 version (no new upstream version), it previously
had no source for the .so files since the Docker build was skipped.

Fix by adding an else branch that:
- Sets z3_version to current_version
- Locates the pre-downloaded libraries in the XDG cache:
    ${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/udb/z3/<version>/<cpu>/libz3.so
- Errors out with a clear message if the cache files are missing
  (directing the user to run 'bin/setup' first)
- Copies them into work_dir as libz3-x64.so / libz3-arm64.so for
  upload to the GitHub Release

Also guard the z3_version.rb update and 'Next steps' output so they
only run when a new upstream version was actually built and released.
